//why: Assigned from what is known about each package, not from what a run did. PyPI records no commit, so every target here needs a tag resolved at minimum; `trivial-deterministic` is reserved for the ones where that resolution is unambiguous and nothing else is required.

labels.reason: Published from a Windows machine: METADATA carries CRLF, which no pinning reproduces from a Linux builder. Handled by the wheel-metadata-eol stabilizer rather than by a repair, but it is a build-environment difference and not a clean deterministic rebuild.
The wheel names setuptools 75.6.0 as its generator; without pinning it, the rebuild uses today's setuptools and METADATA, WHEEL and RECORD all differ.
Built by hatchling 1.29.0. Unpinned it rebuilds under 1.32.0 and diverges on Generator and Metadata-Version alone.
Backend version has to be pinned from the wheel's Generator field.
No rung resolves a usable commit for this version, so no strategy is produced at all. Finding the source is the whole problem here.
An exact tag resolves, and the wheel reproduces byte-for-byte with the backend pinned from its own Generator field. No search of any kind.
Generator says `flit 3.12.0`, but the backend that writes it is flit_core; the distinction has to be known to pin the right package.
setuptools-scm embeds the git commit in _version.py. The publisher built from a tree without git metadata (commit_id = None) and we build from a checkout, so the file differs by construction.
Backend version pinned from the wheel; reproduces once the index is time-filtered.
